key_insight: THReD’s confirmation-gated LLM agent completed 92.7% of preprocessing tasks on its first answer, but completion fell to 58.0% without a data profile.
clinical_relevance: Reliable EHR preprocessing could support clinical AI research, but data-consolidation choices can materially change measured outcomes.
method: Benchmarked 141 tasks across seven categories over 2,550 agent episodes in four context configurations.
Tested preprocessing tools in six experiments using two real chronic-disease cohorts and large-scale synthetic data.
Evaluated reconstruction accuracy, terminology mapping, pipeline reproducibility, subgroup differences and scaling.
evidence_signal: The benchmark reported 92.7% task completion (95% CI 88.1–96.4), 99.0% correct mapping of 2,208 raw variants and byte-identical outputs across 2,176 pipeline replays under pinned dependencies.
watch_item: Performance depended strongly on data-profile context, and same-day consolidation changed 90-day emergency revisit rates by up to 3.2 percentage points.
paper_title: Benchmark of THReD: Evaluating an LLM Agent and Its Preprocessing Tools for Turning Electronic Health Records into AI-Ready Datasets
